chapter: Ch 4: Presentation and Disclosures Based Accounting Standards
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction and Need for Related Party Disclosures
explain: Financial statements normally presume that deals happen at arm's length between independent buyers and sellers.
When parties are related, transactions may occur on special terms, at cost, or even without any charge.
Operating results can be affected by related party relationships even if no actual transactions take place.
AS 18 mandates disclosing related party relationships and transactions to provide a true and fair picture.
This standard applies to standalone financial statements as well as consolidated financial statements of parent entities.

flow.title: Why Related Party Disclosures Are Required
steps: Normal presumption assumes independent arm length transactions
Related parties might influence transaction terms
Transactions may occur at zero price
Relationships can distort reported financial results
Full disclosure ensures transparency for stakeholders

topics.example: A parent company instructs its subsidiary to sell finished goods at direct production cost with zero profit margin.
remember: AS 18 applies to both individual standalone financial statements and group consolidated financial statements.
mistakes: Thinking disclosures are needed only when transactions actually happen, ignoring that mere existence of control requires disclosure.

quiz.q: Why does AS 18 require disclosure of related party relationships?
o: Because related party transactions are strictly illegal in corporate law
Because transactions may not be consummated on an arm's-length basis
To calculate mandatory penalties on inter-company balances
To eliminate the need for preparing consolidated financial statements
quiz.why: Related parties can influence transaction pricing and terms, departing from independent arm's-length conditions.

quiz.q: To which financial statements do the requirements of AS 18 apply?
o: Only standalone statements of listed entities
Only consolidated statements presented by holding companies
Standalone financial statements and consolidated financial statements
Only tax audit reports submitted to revenue authorities
quiz.why: AS 18 applies to each reporting enterprise's financial statements as well as consolidated statements presented by a holding company.

topics.title: Related Party Relationships Covered Under AS 18
explain: AS 18 lists five specific types of relationships to which its provisions exclusively apply.
It includes holding companies, subsidiaries, and fellow subsidiaries under direct or indirect common control.
Associates and joint ventures of the enterprise, along with investing parties, are covered.
Individuals possessing control or significant influence via voting power, plus their relatives, are included.
Key management personnel (KMP) and their relatives are covered related parties.
Enterprises significantly influenced by such individuals or KMP are also treated as related parties.

flow.title: Five Specific Relationships Under AS 18
steps: Direct or indirect parent subsidiary connections
Associates and joint ventures of enterprise
Influential individual voting owners and relatives
Key management personnel and their relatives
Enterprises significantly influenced by owners or KMP

topics.example: A company purchases supplies from a partnership firm owned exclusively by the spouse of its Managing Director.
remember: AS 18 restricts related parties exclusively to five specific statutory categories.
mistakes: Treating an 'associate of an associate' as a related party, which is not covered under AS 18.

quiz.q: Which of the following is explicitly covered as a related party under AS 18?
o: A fellow subsidiary under common control
A non-executive director with zero operational authority
An associate of an associate company
A major customer providing 90% of revenue
quiz.why: Fellow subsidiaries under direct or indirect common control are explicitly included in category (a) of AS 18.

quiz.q: If X Ltd. holds 25% voting power in Y Ltd., and Y Ltd. holds 30% voting power in Z Ltd., is Z Ltd. related to X Ltd. under AS 18?
o: Yes, because indirect significant influence exists throughout
Yes, because both are part of one group
No, because an associate of an associate is not a related party
No, only if X Ltd. disclaims ownership in writing
quiz.why: Under AS 18, an associate of an associate is not deemed to be a related party.

topics.title: Parties Not Deemed to be Related Parties
explain: Two companies sharing a common director are not related parties purely because of that common directorship.
They become related only if the common director actually affects policies of both companies in mutual dealings.
Single customers, suppliers, franchisers, or distributors are not related solely due to economic dependence.
Providers of finance, trade unions, and public utilities are not related parties in their normal dealings.
Government departments and agencies interacting in ordinary course are not deemed related parties.

flow.title: Testing Deemed Non-Related Parties
steps: Identify relationship between external party and enterprise
Check if connection is mere economic dependence
Check if dealing is normal institutional business
Check if common director cannot affect dealings
Conclude party is not a related party

topics.example: A factory buys all electricity from a state electricity board; this does not make the public utility a related party.
remember: Economic dependence alone never establishes a related party relationship under AS 18.
mistakes: Assuming that sharing a common director automatically makes two separate companies related parties.

quiz.q: Under AS 18, two companies having a director in common are considered related parties when:
o: They share an office premises
The director affects policies of both companies in mutual dealings
Both companies are registered in the same state
They belong to the same manufacturing sector
quiz.why: A common director creates a related party relationship only if that person can influence mutual dealing policies.

quiz.q: Which of the following is deemed NOT to be a related party in normal course of dealings?
o: Key management personnel
Subsidiary company
Provider of finance
Holding company
quiz.why: Providers of finance acting in normal commercial course are deemed not to be related parties.

topics.title: Exemptions From Related Party Disclosures
explain: Disclosures are exempt if they conflict with statutory confidentiality duties imposed by law or a regulatory authority.
For example, banks cannot be forced by AS 18 to break banking secrecy laws regarding client transactions.
Confidentiality clauses in purely commercial contracts do NOT provide any exemption from AS 18 disclosure.
In consolidated financial statements, intra-group transactions between group members are completely exempt.
State-controlled enterprises are exempt from disclosing transactions with other state-controlled enterprises.

flow.title: Evaluating Exemption Applicability
steps: Identify potential related party transaction for reporting
Check if statutory duty of secrecy applies
Check if intra-group entry in consolidated statements
Check if transaction between state-controlled enterprises
Apply disclosure exemption if criteria are met

topics.example: A bank is prohibited by statute from revealing customer transaction details, so AS 18 disclosures do not override this duty.
remember: Private commercial non-disclosure agreements do NOT exempt an entity from AS 18 disclosures.
mistakes: Claiming exemption under AS 18 based on private contractual confidentiality agreements.

quiz.q: Can ABC Ltd. withhold related party disclosures citing a confidentiality clause in a private commercial agreement?
o: Yes, private contracts override accounting standards
Yes, if approved by its statutory auditor
No, exemption applies only to statutory confidentiality duties
No, unless the counterparty is a foreign entity
quiz.why: Exemption applies only where disclosure conflicts with duties imposed by a statute or regulator, not commercial contracts.

quiz.q: Are intra-group transactions disclosed in consolidated financial statements under AS 18?
o: Yes, all intra-group transactions must be disclosed
No, intra-group transactions are exempt from consolidated disclosures
Only transactions exceeding 10% of revenue need disclosure
Yes, but only if they are conducted at cost
quiz.why: Consolidated financial statements view the group as a single enterprise, making intra-group disclosures unnecessary.

topics.title: Definitions: Control, Significant Influence, and Associate
explain: Control means direct or indirect ownership of more than one-half of the voting power of an enterprise.
Control also exists through power over board composition to appoint or remove majority directors without concurrence.
Control also means substantial interest (20% or more voting power) combined with power to direct operating policies.
Significant influence means participation in financial or operating policy decisions without having control.
Significant influence is presumed if an investor holds 20% or more of voting power directly or indirectly.
An associate is an enterprise where an investor has significant influence, excluding subsidiaries and joint ventures.

flow.title: Determining Control vs Significant Influence
steps: Check voting power percentage held in investee
If voting power exceeds 50 percent, control exists
If board appointment power exists, control exists
If voting power is 20 percent to 50 percent, influence presumed
Classify as subsidiary for control or associate for influence

topics.example: A company owning 24% voting rights in an investee is presumed to have significant influence, making the investee an associate.
remember: Control under AS 18 includes substantial interest (>=20%) plus policy direction power, wider than AS 21.
mistakes: Assuming significant influence requires majority ownership, when 20% voting power triggers the legal presumption.

quiz.q: Under AS 18, holding what percentage of voting power creates a presumption of significant influence?
o: 10% or more
20% or more
More than 50%
At least 75%
quiz.why: AS 18 presumes significant influence if an investing party holds 20% or more of the voting power.

quiz.q: How does the definition of control in AS 18 compare to AS 21?
o: It is narrower than AS 21
It is identical to AS 21 in all respects
It is wider because clause (c) adds substantial interest with power to direct policies
It excludes voting rights held through subsidiaries
quiz.why: AS 18 has an extra clause (c) covering substantial interest plus contractual or statutory policy control.

topics.title: Definitions: KMP, Relatives, and Other Entities
explain: Key Management Personnel (KMP) have authority and responsibility for planning, directing, and controlling operations.
Examples of KMP include managing directors, whole-time directors, managers, and directing executive officers.
A non-executive director is NOT a KMP merely by virtue of directorship unless operational authority is proven.
A relative of an individual includes spouse, son, daughter, brother, sister, father, and mother.
A joint venture is a contractual arrangement where two or more parties undertake an economic activity with joint control.
Joint control is the contractually agreed sharing of governing power and does not depend on voting power percentages.

flow.title: Identifying KMP and Related Individuals
steps: Identify person with planning and directing authority
Include Managing Director, Whole-time Director, or Manager
Exclude ordinary non-executive independent board directors
Identify relatives: spouse, parents, children, siblings
Tag these individuals as related parties

topics.example: The managing director of a company along with their spouse and brother are classified as related parties under AS 18.
remember: AS 18 relative list: spouse, son, daughter, brother, sister, father, mother.
mistakes: Assuming non-executive directors are automatically KMP without verifying operational management authority.

quiz.q: Which of the following family members is NOT listed as a 'relative' under AS 18?
o: Brother
Sister
Uncle
Mother
quiz.why: AS 18 defines relative strictly as spouse, son, daughter, brother, sister, father, and mother.

quiz.q: Is a non-executive director automatically classified as Key Management Personnel under AS 18?
o: Yes, all board members are automatically KMP
No, unless they possess operational planning and directing authority
Yes, if they attend more than three board meetings
No, non-executive directors can never be related parties under any clause
quiz.why: A non-executive director is not KMP merely by directorship unless they actually have executive planning authority.

topics.title: Disclosure Requirements and Rules Under AS 18
explain: If control exists, the related party's name and relationship must be disclosed even if zero transactions took place.
When transactions take place, disclosures must specify the party name, relationship description, and transaction nature.
Disclosures must state the volume of transactions, outstanding balances, and provisions for doubtful debts.
Amounts written off or written back regarding debts from or to related parties must be reported.
Disclosures apply to transactions occurring during the period the related party relationship actually existed.
Remuneration paid to key management personnel is a related party transaction requiring clear disclosure.

flow.title: Disclosure Assessment Process
steps: Check if relationship involves control
Disclose name and relationship even without transactions
Identify all transactions during existence of relationship
Exclude transactions occurring after relationship ended
Disclose volume, outstanding balances, and write-offs

topics.example: A firm sold goods to an associate for 3 months before divesting its stake; only sales during those 3 months are disclosed.
remember: Transactions are reported only for the period during which the related party relationship existed.
mistakes: Disclosing transactions for the whole year when the related party relationship existed only for a partial period.

quiz.q: If control exists between two enterprises, what must be disclosed when no transactions took place during the year?
o: No disclosure is required at all
A nil balance financial certificate
Name of related party and nature of relationship
Estimated fair value of non-occurring transactions
quiz.why: Where control exists, name and nature of relationship must be disclosed regardless of whether transactions occurred.

quiz.q: P Ltd. owned an associate up to 30 June 20X1 and sold goods to it before and after that date. What must be disclosed under AS 18 for the year ended 31 March 20X2?
o: Transactions for the entire 12-month financial year
Only transactions entered into up to 30 June 20X1
Only transactions entered into after 30 June 20X1
No transactions need to be disclosed since the relationship ended
quiz.why: Disclosures under AS 18 are required only for transactions during the period the relationship actually existed.
